items.title: Adnex bags Bursa building refurbishment job
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Adnex Group Bhd's wholly owned unit Adnex Interior Solution Sdn Bhd has secured a contract from Bursa Malaysia Bhd for refurbishment works at its Exchange Square main building. Adnex said the RM14.19 million contract, accepted on Oct 2, covers refurbishment works at levels six, 14 and 15 of the building. Managing director Adrian Kan Wai Chun said the latest contract was the second purchase order Adnex had received from Bursa Malaysia, following refurbishment works at the Exchange Square public listing gallery earlier this year.

items.title: HKL emergency dept upgrade enters final phase, completion targeted by end-2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The upgrading project of the new block of the Emergency and Trauma Department at the Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) is now in the final phase of implementation. The HKL Management said today that several issues require repair and improvement work in the inspection and completion process before the facility can be fully completed. HKL said that it is committed to ensuring that all repair work is carried out properly to meet the facility’s safety, functional, and quality requirements before the project is finalised.

items.title: Petronas Chemicals appoints Izwan Ismail as MD, CEO effective Jan 1, 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd (PetChem) has appointed Izwan Ismail as managing director (MD) and chief executive officer (CEO) effective Jan 1, 2027. PetChem said Izwan, 51, brings over 29 years of experience spanning finance, corporate planning, strategy, commercial management, operations and technology. "Currently he serves as director of Petronas Gas Bhd and various subsidiaries of the Petronas Group," it said.

items.title: Jobbie, Lotus's target RM20,000 for Makna
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian peanut butter brand Jobbie and Lotus's Malaysia are expanding their breast health awareness campaign. The campaign, running from Oct 1 to Dec 31, involves 20,000 specially designed jars, targeting RM20,000 in contributions to support cancer patients. The campaign jars feature illustrations and information on common breast cancer signs and symptoms, aiming to encourage conversations about breast health at home.

items.title: KL woman fined RM24,000 over fraudulent transfer of retiree’s RM1.1m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — An unemployed woman was fined RM24,000 by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to two charges of fraudulently transferring RM1.1 million belonging to a retiree into her own bank account eight years ago. Judge Muhammad Ilmami Ahmad imposed the fine on Chin Chew Woon, 43, and ordered her to serve 24 months’ imprisonment if she failed to settle the fine. According to the charges, Chin was accused of transferring RM500,000 and RM600,000 belonging to a 66-year-old man into her bank account in Brickfields on December 26 and 27, 2018.

items.title: Air quality improves nationwide, no unhealthy readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality improved nationwide amid transboundary haze, with no areas recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5.30pm today. According to the Department of Environment's (DoE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 65 areas recorded moderate air quality, while three were in the good category. Cheras in Kuala Lumpur recorded the highest API reading at 96, followed by Sri Manjung, Sri Aman and Serian in Sarawak, each at 92.

items.title: Zetrix AI tumbles 33pct, closes at 11 sen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd shares plunged 33 per cent on Friday, closing at 12 sen after a report said the company owes the government more than RM200 million in unremitted collections. The counter fell 5.5 sen from Thursday's close of 16.5 sen, after opening at 16.5 sen and touching an intraday low of 10 sen. Zetrix AI, formerly known as MyEG Services Bhd, was a pioneer in providing online government services through its link-up with RTD.

items.title: Lee had space to speak, but did not use it, says PKR deputy sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Petaling Jaya member of parliament Lee Chean Chung had the opportunity to voice his views within PKR but did not attend most of the party's central leadership council meetings since November. He said Lee, who was elected to the MPP, later chose to resign from the party leadership council. Ng also disputed Lee's claim that he was unable to raise issues affecting Petaling Jaya, saying Lee had been invited to meetings on flood mitigation by the Petaling Jaya City Council (MBPJ) and at state level, but did not attend most of them.

items.title: JPJ suspends all MYEG Group services from Oct 5 over unresolved contractual obligations
items.summary: In a statement today, JPJ said the suspension covers My E.G. As a result, all JPJ services currently available through MYEG Group channels will be suspended from October 5. Vehicle ownership transfers can meanwhile be carried out through JPJ counters, selected kiosks, the JPJ public portal and eAuto for certain transactions.

items.title: PSD awaits Home Ministry probe before deciding on MCBA DG viral incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Service Department (PSD) will await the outcome of the Home Ministry's investigation before deciding on the next course of action over a viral incident involving Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain. Its director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said the department had yet to receive any report against the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency director-general over his actions in the viral clip showing him berating two men. "So far, the department has yet to receive any report on the viral issue involving the MCBA director-general.

items.title: 155 firefighters, 12 assets deployed for Bahrain F1 Grand Prix in Malaysia
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A total of 155 Fire and Rescue Department personnel and 12 assets have been mobilised to ensure emergency and rescue preparedness throughout the Gulf Air Bahrain Formula 1 (F1) Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC). "Among the assets deployed are a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT), two Compact Fire Rescue Tenders (CFRT), a 10,000-litre water tanker, three Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) ambulances and four department buses. Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the deployment reflected the department's commitment to supporting international events while prioritising safety and emergency preparedness.

items.title: Johor-Singapore RTS Link passenger service to start in February 2027
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Passenger service on the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link is expected to begin in February 2027, with all system tests and trial runs targeted for completion by Dec 31. "Our goal is to provide a safe and reliable service on the RTS Link," it said. The RTS Link, a bilateral project between Malaysia and Singapore, will connect Bukit Chagar in Johor Baru with Woodlands North in Singapore.

items.title: RM5,000 trial payout leads Pontian victim into RM1.15m investment scam
items.summary: PONTIAN, Oct 2 — A private-sector employee lost RM1.15 million after falling victim to an online investment scam operated by a syndicate. Pontian District Police Chief Supt Hadzrat Hussein Mion Hussain said police received a report from the 52-year-old man yesterday, with preliminary investigations finding that the incident began in early January after he got acquainted with a woman via WhatsApp. “Convinced by the investment, the victim subsequently made several more transactions to several bank accounts in stages until March 26, 2026, involving a total of RM1,151,621.96,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: JB-Singapore RTS Link service start pushed back to February 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Passenger service on the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link is now expected to begin in February 2027, the Malaysian and Singaporean governments said today. In a joint statement, the Land Transport Authority of Singapore (Singapore Grantor) and the Ministry of Transport Malaysia (Malaysia Grantor) said they had been informed by RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO) of the revised timeline. The new target is subject to RTSO obtaining independent safety certification for the RTS Link and securing final regulatory approvals.

items.title: Johor conservation efforts produce about 5,000 turtle hatchlings a year
items.summary: Johor Department of Fisheries director Rosmawati Ghazali said the main turtle nesting sites identified include Pulau Apil, Pulau Dayang, Pulau Besar and Pulau Tinggi here. However, Rosmawati said turtle eggs left to hatch naturally face a high risk of predation, so they transfer eggs found at nesting sites to hatcheries for closer monitoring. Therefore, we transfer eggs found at nesting sites to hatcheries so our personnel can monitor them more closely,” she said.

items.title: MCMC, MACC to use AI in fight against corruption and abuse of power
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, Oct 2 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will leverage artificial intelligence (AI) technology to detect, prevent and manage the risks of abuse of power and misappropriation more systematically and effectively. In a statement today, MCMC said this was among the areas of collaboration agreed upon by the two agencies through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen strategic cooperation in enforcement, corruption prevention and integrity empowerment in addressing complex challenges in the digital environment. The exchange of the MoU between MCMC chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din and MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman took place at the MCMC headquarters here today.

items.title: Mark your calendars: Syed Saddiq, Bella invite all to wedding receptions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and artiste Bella Astillah have invited the public to their wedding receptions in Muar, Johor, and Kota Kinabalu, Sabah. The receptions will be held on Oct 25 and 31 respectively. The receptions will follow their solemnisation ceremony, which will take place on Oct 10.

items.title: Department mobilises 153 firefighters, medevac teams and buses to ensure optimum safety during F1
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — A total of 155 officers and members, along with 12 assets from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), have been deployed to ensure that the levels of safety, emergency preparedness, and rescue operations are at an optimum level throughout the hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026, scheduled to take place at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC). “The assignment of JBPM officers, personnel, and assets to strategic locations is to ensure that any emergency and rescue needs can be addressed quickly, orderly and effectively,” he said in a statement today. He said that 12 departmental assets are being mobilised throughout the event, comprising a Fire Rescue Tender, two Compact Fire Rescue Tenders, one 10,000-litre water tanker, three Emergency Medical Rescue Services ambulances and four JBPM buses.

items.title: Anwar secures fast-track process for missing Malaysians in Nepal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah has assured Malaysia of full cooperation to determine the status of 54 citizens still missing after devastating floods and landslides in Nepal, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. He is willing to give all the cooperation,” Anwar said to reporters this afternoon, adding that Shah agreed during a bilateral call to facilitate administrative and legal efforts to help relatives obtain closure as quickly as possible. The standard legal procedures in Nepal typically require a three-year waiting period to issue a death certificate for missing persons, compared to six or seven years under Malaysian law, Anwar said.

items.title: Police arrest 13 in Teluk Intan raids, syndicate used Alipay accounts to move gambling proceeds
items.summary: TELUK INTAN, Oct 2 — Police have arrested 13 people over a syndicate that allegedly used Alipay accounts opened with Malaysians’ passport details to receive and transfer proceeds from online gambling scams targeting Chinese nationals. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspects, comprising five Malaysians and eight Myanmar nationals aged between 20 and 44, were arrested in two raids here on Sept 28. Mohd Alwi said the syndicate, believed to have been operating since mid-July, had opened about 60 Alipay accounts using the personal details of local residents.

items.title: Masseur gets 20 months' jail, two strokes for molesting customer
items.summary: Magistrate Marilyn Kelvin sentenced Ahmad Johan Yong Abdullah @ Yong Kui Fook, 31, after he pleaded guilty to the charge. According to the facts of the case,Johan repeatedly touched the victim inappropriately despite being told to stop. The victim, who felt uncomfortable with Johan's actions, subsequently lodged a police report.

items.title: RTD suspends MYEG, Zetrix as collection agents from Oct 5
items.summary: For Malaysian driving licence (CDL) renewals, the available channels are RTD counters, MyJPJ, RTD Public Portal, RTD kiosks, RTD Mobile counters and Pos Malaysia outlets. Applications for Malaysian Learner Driving Licences (LDL) can be made through RTD counters, MyJPJ, RTD Public Portal, RTD kiosks and RTD Mobile counters. For summons checks and payments, the public can use RTD counters, MyJPJ, RTD Public Portal, RTD kiosks and RTD Mobile counters.

items.title: Court of Appeal overturns acquittal, jails ex‑bowling coach two more years for molesting 13‑year‑old
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — A former bowling coach, already serving a prison term for sexual assault, was sentenced to an additional two years’ imprisonment by the Court of Appeal today for molesting another former Malaysia Games male athlete in 2017. A three-member bench led by Federal Court judge Datuk Azmi Ariffin, sitting as a Court of Appeal judge, ordered Mat Salleh Jalani to begin serving the two-year sentence after completing his six-year prison term for sexually assaulting a 14-year-old male athlete in 2018. The court reinstated the Magistrates’ Court’s conviction and increased the sentence from 18 months to two years’ imprisonment.

items.title: Damai Perdana residents seek official safety assurance after landslide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Residents of Pangsapuri Damai Perdana 2 have demanded an official explanation from management and local authorities regarding building safety, following a notice allowing them to return home starting today. Block D resident Lina Ridzuan, 43, said the permission letter issued by the local authority lacked concrete safety guarantees and basic utility restoration. she said.

items.title: 14-year-old teenager sexually assaulted by man at PPR
items.summary: Cheras deputy police chief Superintendent Lim Chun How said the case came to light following a report lodged by the teenager's mother on Sept 29. "Police confirm receiving a report from the victim's mother concerning the sexual assault of her son. The victim's mother lodged a police report after her son confided in her.

items.title: Keep fighting until final whistle, Anwar tells Harimau Malaya
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on the Harimau Malaya squad to maintain its winning momentum in the Fifa Asean Cup 2026 third-place playoff on Monday. In a Facebook post today, Anwar said the fighting spirit and determination shown by the national squad throughout the campaign remained a source of pride for Malaysians despite missing out on the final. Maintain the momentum, fight until the final whistle and bring home a victory for Malaysia!

items.title: Physiotherapist recalls emotional moment beside grieving Dr M
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A physiotherapist who was seen crying beside Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad during his wife's funeral said he was deeply moved by the former prime minister's grief. "Seeing Tun M (Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad) in such a state of sadness moved me so deeply that I shed tears," said Kevin Choo, 31. Choo's presence beside Dr Mahathir during the funeral of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, on Monday drew attention on social media after he was seen crying alongside the former prime minister.

items.title: Thunderstorms expected in KL, Selangor and nine states until 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for multiple states across Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, and Sabah, forecasting heavy downpours, lightning, and gusty winds until 7pm today. In the weather advisory issued at 4pm, MetMalaysia indicated that the adverse weather will affect the entire northern states of Perlis, Kedah, Penang, and Perak, alongside the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. In Selangor, seven districts are on alert: Petaling, Sepang, Kuala Selangor, Sabak Bernam, Klang, Kuala Langat, and Gombak.

items.title: Ahmad Maslan urges BN to announce Melaka candidates early, give time to meet voters
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Oct 2 — Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan has suggested that Barisan Nasional (BN) announce its candidate list for the Melaka state election early. Ahmad, who is also Umno War Room Secretariat chief, said an early announcement would give shortlisted candidates sufficient time to prepare and introduce themselves to voters. Ahmad, who is also Deputy Public Works Minister, said BN’s candidates for the Melaka state election would undergo three levels of screening before a final decision is made by the party’s top leadership.

items.title: No media ban at Siti Hasmah grave visit, Media Club lodges police report over doctored photo
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: There was no official restriction or ban on media coverage when former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad visited the grave of his late wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, at Pusara Negara here yesterday, says Putrajaya Media Club (KMP). KMP said media personnel covering the visit were aware of their journalistic ethics and the need to respect human values, privacy and the family's sensitivities while carrying out their professional duties in a sombre setting. "KMP wishes to stress that media personnel did not receive any official notification of restrictions or a ban on recording from Dr Mahathir's office or family at the location.

items.title: Driver fined RM1,000 for using criminal force on sister's ex-boyfriend at nasi kandar shop
items.summary: Muhammad Zulhafiz Muhammad Zahari, 30, pleaded guilty to using criminal force against his sister's former boyfriend, 24-year-old parcel delivery man Muhammad Afiff Zahran Zori, without grave and sudden provocation. However, the meeting turned heated when Zulhafiz accused Afiff of assaulting his sister. Zulhafiz then choked Afiff before the situation was brought under control by Afiff's family members and other diners.

items.title: Akmal welcomes Pas's readiness to use BN logo in Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA: Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhammad Akmal Saleh has welcomed Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang's statement expressing readiness to use the Barisan Nasional symbol in the Melaka election if cooperation is finalised. He said the development was seen as an effort that could open wider avenues towards strengthening cooperation and Muslim unity ahead of the Melaka state polls. Earlier, Hadi was reported as saying that Pas was prepared to use the BN symbol in the Melaka election.

items.title: Affordable housing to affordable living: Hopes for 2027 budget
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: For many Malaysians, affordability is no longer just about buying a home. The Ministry of Finance's Pre-Budget Statement places homeownership and rental affordability alongside public transport, urban liveability, and wider household cost pressures, from transport to healthcare, education, and childcare. Recognising Rental Affordability as Part of Malaysia's Housing Agenda Rental is an increasingly important part of how Malaysians navigate the housing market.

items.title: Ravindran: Lift SST on residential security
items.summary: Families living in landed homes are paying private security guards to protect their streets, homes and children. Yet on every ringgit they contribute towards this basic protection, they are also charged 8.0 per cent Service Tax. Exempt security and guard services paid by residents of landed housing estates from the Service Tax.

items.title: Fadhlina urges victims in freelance speaker case to lodge reports
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: The Education Ministry has urged victims in the case involving a freelance speaker accused of inappropriate conduct to come forward and lodge reports with the authorities to facilitate investigations. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said such reports were crucial to enable the authorities to investigate the allegations and allow the ministry to take appropriate action through established procedures. Also present was Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan.

items.title: Beware of ticket touts cashing in on F1, MotoGP, says Fuziah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The public should remain vigilant against ticket touts seeking to cash in on several world-class events being held in Malaysia throughout October. Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said Malaysia would host several international events this month, including the Gulf Air Bahrain Formula 1 (F1) Grand Prix Malaysia 2026, which begins tomorrow. "More worryingly, purchasing tickets through unofficial sellers could expose us to scams.

items.title: KL Marathon goes ahead this weekend, but Kids Dash cancelled over haze concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 – The Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon (KLSCM) 2026 will proceed this weekend despite the haze, but organisers have cancelled the Kids Dash races to protect the health of young participants. In a race update, organisers said the Full Marathon, ASICS Half Marathon, IHH 10km and 5km will run as scheduled. “We regret to announce that the Kids Dash races will be cancelled, in the best interest of the children,” the organisers said.

items.title: Anwar calls for swift refurbishment of RMAF quarters at Sungai Besi land
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for the refurbishment of the former Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) quarters at Sungai Besi Land to be expedited. KLCC Development Sdn Bhd head Wan Shamilah Wan Muhammad Saidi said the project involved refurbishing two former RMAF apartment blocks comprising 160 units, or 80 units per block. KLCC Development Sdn Bhd head Wan Shamilah Wan Muhammad Saidi said the project involved refurbishing two former RMAF apartment blocks comprising 160 units, or 80 units per block.

items.title: Homeowners in UK and beyond hit as global bond selloff drives up mortgage costs
items.summary: LONDON: For five years, the interest rate on Richard Merrett's mortgage was locked at 1.14 per cent, but with that ultra-cheap deal due to expire in early 2027 he faces a sudden trebling of his monthly housing costs from £550 (US$728) a month to £1,650. Merrett is no stranger to the risks in the lending market — he is managing director at mortgage firm Alexander Hall. BORROWERS FACE MOUNTING PRESSURES The rise in Britain's 30-year government bond yield , which topped 6.0 per cent on Thursday for the first time since 1998, will further increase mortgage rates as banks pass on the increased cost of funding to homebuyers, said Nicholas Mendes, mortgage manager at broker John Charcol.

items.title: State governments urged to gazette paddy land as rice self‑sufficiency drops to 54.3pc
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — State governments have been urged to gazette paddy-growing areas to sustain rice cultivation and strengthen the country’s food security after the rice self-sufficiency ratio (SSR) declined last year. According to the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry (KPKM), the proposal was among the matters discussed at the second 2026 Agriculture and Food Security Ministers’ Meeting with state agriculture executive councillors, chaired by Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu yesterday. “Malaysia’s reliance on imported rice was estimated at 1.416 million metric tonnes, worth RM2.953 billion, in 2025,” KPKM said in a statement today.

items.title: Immigration turns up the heat on tomyam restaurants
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The Immigration Department will step up enforcement at tomyam restaurants, including in Kelantan, following a claim by Thai authorities that about 100,000 workers at such eateries in Malaysia do not have valid work permits. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department took note of the claim. His statement follows a claim by Thai authorities that about 100,000 workers at tomyam restaurants in Malaysia were working without valid permits.

items.title: Lorry driver jailed 11 years for killing man over wife lookalike remark
items.summary: B. Satiasarma, 41, and the victim, S. Sarathi, 20, had gone to a drug-taking spot at a palm oil plantation in Simpang Halt, near here, on April 30 last year. According to the grounds of judgment by High Court judicial commissioner Syed Faisal Syed Amir, Satiasarma had heard a rumour that Sarathi was having an affair with his wife. While they were at the location, Sarathi told Satiasarma that he had had sex with a woman whose characteristics were similar to those of Satiasarma's wife.

items.title: Jobless man charged with misappropriating RM2,783 from customer
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: An unemployed man was charged in the magistrate's court here today with misappropriating RM2,783.90 belonging to a customer of a money-changing company in March. C. Narendran, 35, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read out to him before magistrate A. Shaarmini. According to the charge, Narendran was accused of dishonestly converting RM2,783.90 belonging to a 32-year-old woman to his own use.

items.title: Proton blows past 2025 sales in nine months
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Proton Holdings Bhd has surpassed its full-year 2025 sales target in just nine months, with year-to-date (YTD) sales reaching 160,886 units as of September. Proton said September sales rose 45 per cent year-on-year to 19,465 units, bringing YTD sales growth to 40.8 per cent. Meanwhile, Proton S70 sales stood at 2,756 units in September, taking its YTD total to 20,709 units and surpassing its full-year 2025 sales.

items.title: MCMC probes AI‑manipulated footage of Dr Mahathir grieving wife’s death, warns of legal action
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has its eyes on social media content that allegedly uses artificial intelligence (AI) to manipulate footage of Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad grieving the death of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali. The commission said it had contacted the relevant social media platforms over the content. Suspected manipulated content should also be reported to the relevant platforms or authorities.

items.title: Safe return of solo Malaysian after 37 days in Nepal floods offers hope to 54 still missing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — One of the 55 Malaysians reported to have lost contact following floods and landslides in Nepal last August has been confirmed safe and has returned to Malaysia. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the man went to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu on his own yesterday before departing for home and arriving in the country this morning. He said this development means 54 Malaysians remain missing, with all of them travelling in separate groups.

items.title: Anwar: Lee Chean Chung effectively quit PKR for ‘sometime already’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Prime Minister and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today alleged Lee Chean Chung had been an absentee leader, failing to attend meetings or even the party congress “for over a year”. Lee announced his resignation as Petaling Jaya MP this morning, a move that followed a three year suspension for insubordination. Lee said he would tender his resignation from PKR this Monday.

items.title: Flood mitigation remains Batu pond’s priority as Petra explores supplying 10 million litres daily
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The Batu flood retention pond could be upgraded into a dual-purpose facility that retains its flood mitigation role while providing up to 10 million litres of alternative water supply daily. The Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry (Petra) said the proposed pilot project would provide five million litres per day (MLD) for domestic use, potentially benefiting about 6,000 homes, and another 5 MLD for industrial use in the Batu area. Petra said the project was in line with the National Water Policy’s aim of strengthening water security through more efficient, sustainable and resilient water resource management.

items.title: Tourism Malaysia reports 28.8 million international arrivals Jan–Aug, sector shows steady growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Malaysia’s tourism sector continues to show positive momentum by recording 28.8 million international visitors from January to August this year, a 1.8 per cent increase compared to the same period last year. Tourism Malaysia deputy director-general (promotion) Mohd Akbal Setia said the positive performance reflects the continued appeal of Malaysia as a tourism destination and the importance of strengthening international tourism partnerships. He said this when delivering a speech on behalf of Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing at the opening of the International Tourism, Arts and Culture Exhibition and Conference (INTACT) 2026 at Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here today.

items.title: Bahrain Crown Prince lands in Malaysia for Sepang F1 Grand Prix weekend
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 2 — The Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Bahrain, Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, arrived in Malaysia today for a special visit in conjunction with the Formula One (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang International Circuit (SIC), which kicks off today. On hand to welcome the Crown Prince were Tunku Temenggong Johor Tunku Idris Iskandar Al-Haj Sultan Ibrahim, Tunku Panglima Johor Tunku Abdul Rahman Al-Haj Sultan Ibrahim, and Tunku Putera Johor Tunku Abu Bakar Al-Haj Sultan Ibrahim. Also present were Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari and Bahrain’s Ambassador to Malaysia Dr Waleed Khalifa Al Manea.

items.title: Ministry confirms RM200m arrears owed by Zetrix AI, formerly MyEG, over road tax and licence fees
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The Ministry of Transport has confirmed that digital services company Zetrix AI Bhd owes the federal government over RM200 million in unremitted public collections. Earlier, the Singapore daily reported, citing official government documents, that Zetrix AI had withheld the collections from the very inception of its three-year service contract in May 2023. An unnamed government official said the ministry was weighing its options.

items.title: Raub police assault: Two Myanmar nationals charged over serious injury to corporal
items.summary: RAUB, Oct 2 — Two Myanmar nationals were brought before the Sessions Court here today to face a joint charge of causing injury to a policeman last month. Judge Siti Hajar Mustaffa then set Oct 14 for case mention to allow a Myanmar interpreter to be present in court. The court also denied bail to both men.

items.title: It’s live! Anwar says RTM to show Bahrain F1 GP Malaysia is hosting this weekend
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The 2026 Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix, which Malaysia is hosting this weekend, will be broadcast live on RTM, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today. He said the live telecast would give Malaysians the chance to experience the thrill of a world-class race, with the event taking place at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), Bernama reported. RTM will broadcast the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 live in Malaysia so that the excitement of this race can be enjoyed together.

items.title: Selangor expands RM30 monthly transport subsidy to KTM Komuter services, effective immediately
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 2 — The Selangor state government has expanded its RM30 Monthly Selangor Public Transport Subsidy to KTM Komuter services, effective immediately. State Investment, Trade and Mobility Committee chairman Ng Sze Han said the expansion would enable more users to benefit from the subsidy, which initially covered Rapid KL On-Demand and Kumpool services. Applicants must be registered voters in Selangor.

items.title: Hadi: PAS still open to BN pact for Melaka polls, ready to contest under own logo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — PAS is adamant in rejecting any political cooperation with Pakatan Harapan (PH) for the Melaka state election, while staying open to electoral pacts that ensure a Malay-Muslim administration in the state, said party president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang. We reject Pakatan Harapan,” he said. The Melaka State Legislative Assembly was dissolved on September 23, paving the way for snap state polls.

items.title: Court of Appeal overturns High Court acquittal, health officer ordered to enter defence on seven unnatural sex charges
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — The Court of Appeal yesterday overturned a High Court decision acquitting a health officer of seven charges of having unnatural sex with a woman and ordered him to enter his defence. “The High Court’s order upholding the decision of the Sessions Court is set aside. The decision was subsequently upheld by the Kota Bharu High Court.

items.title: Power to the people: TNB gives pro‑rata credits, 800kWh households enjoy full exemptions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Tenaga Nasional Bhd’s (TNB) customers who use up to 800 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of electricity per month will receive a pro-rata credit for the September bill adjustment, which will be credited directly to their October 2026 electricity bills. “With this, domestic customers with monthly consumption of 800 kWh or less from Sept 1-Dec 31, 2026 will enjoy full exemption from the automatic fuel adjustment (AFA) charge, the RM10 retail charge and the eight per cent service tax. “The adjusted amount will be shown on customers’ bills under the descriptions ‘Bill Adjustment (Sept 2026)’ and ‘Service Tax Adjustment (8.0 per cent) (Sept 2026)’,” TNB said in a statement today.

items.title: Setapak Jaya demolition: Afdlin Shauki says relocation deal safeguards livelihoods of affected traders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The relocation of 98 traders from the Seri Semarak Small and Medium Industry (SMI) premises in Setapak Jaya is moving towards a resolution, with the developer offering ex-gratia payments and relocation assistance while three alternative sites have been identified. Setiawangsa Parliamentary Zone Coordinator Datuk Afdlin Shauki Aksan said the commitments were reached through intensive negotiations involving various parties, including government agencies and developer 59 Inc Sdn Bhd. He said the 98 affected business operators, who have operated in the area for 31 years, would be able to choose from three alternative sites owned by the Land and Mines Office (PTG).

items.title: Refusing to ‘sit silently’, Lee Chean Chung quits as Petaling Jaya MP over PKR suspension
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 2 — Lee Chean Chung has announced his immediate resignation as the member of parliament for Petaling Jaya, saying he refuses to draw a lawmaker's salary while being sidelined. “Therefore, I, Lee Chean Chung, have today decided to resign unconditionally as the Member of Parliament for Petaling Jaya,” he said. Lee also said he would submit his resignation from PKR by Monday.
